method: Sum completed native invocation wall windows for the same three interfaces. Categories and roles are separate work, which overlaps; sums are not elapsed turnaround or pure reasoning. Different packets, scene coverage and resume history prevent causal attribution.

The single staged trim changes Coast montage from Start 04 / inclusive End 12 to Start 02 / inclusive End 15, then trim-applied commits both boundary changes and the City lights shift as one Undo operation. The assigned /actions/10 canonical interaction specifies trimming Start or End and explicitly keeps timeline End fixed during a Start trim. No intermediate interaction explains two separate boundary edits. The rendered example therefore demonstrates a different trim operation from the supplied source.

The source defines inclusive End boundaries, but the resulting clips are labeled Coast shore 04–08 and Coast walk 08–12, sharing frame 08 under that convention. In addition, excluded-note calls source intro 00–04 and outro 12–16 wholly excluded even though they meet the retained group's inclusive 04–12 interval at frames 04 and 12. No distinction between geometric cut positions and inclusive frame timestamps is supplied. Consequently the central visible-only Ungroup example does not establish nonoverlapping parts or correct preservation of the boundary frames required by /actions/27.

No rendered state depicts that menu context. This is an inherited wireframe/source mismatch, not a new theme defect.

The rendered trim-preview scene simultaneously shows focus outlines on Select assembly A (select-group), Apply trim (trim-end), and Assembly A (group-a). These nodes all retain state:'focus'. Similar conflicting focus targets occur in group-selected and its inherited result/cancellation scenes, in ungroup-failure where selection-actions adds another focus outline, and in ungrouped where both select-part-b and part-b are focused. Selection is already represented by variant:'selected', so the extra focus states imply multiple current keyboard targets and make the command activated from the keyboard ambiguous. This also prevents a coherent reading of the stated failure focus intent.

The newly explicit one-frame-per-second, inclusive-End convention conflicts with the occupied clip geometry. Part B is described as containing frames 10–13 and Part C as starting on the immediately following frame 14, but their rectangles use scalePosition 10→13 and 14→18. The actual screenshot therefore shows an empty track interval between the parts, while separate-detail and separate-status call them adjacent. The same mismatch appears in trim-preview and trim-applied: Assembly A's rectangle ends at 24 and Arrival B starts at 25, leaving a visible gap although the new text says the clips are adjacent. At the declared rate, each included frame occupies one second; mapping the last included frame's timestamp directly to the rectangle's right edge omits that final frame's occupied span. This misrepresents preserved timing after Ungroup and the result of the collision push.

The selected assembly explicitly uses inclusive End 18s, but the Ungroup result labels adjacent parts as Part B 10–14s and Part C 14–18s, with both structured intervals meeting at 14. Under the displayed inclusive-End convention, this assigns the 14s boundary frame to both parts; an exclusive-end interpretation would be an unexplained convention change. The result therefore does not unambiguously demonstrate the required nonoverlapping parts with preserved timing. The shared scale aligns the coordinates but does not resolve their frame semantics.
